rows.sourceTitle: Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Bronchiectasis: Prevalence, Risk Factors and Clinical Implications-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.implementationCitation: Srivali N, De Giacomi F. Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Bronchiectasis: Prevalence, Risk Factors and Clinical Implications-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Sleep Res. 2026;35(4):e70333. PMID 41905893. doi:10.1111/jsr.70333.
rows.finalCitation: Srivali N, De Giacomi F. Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Bronchiectasis: Prevalence, Risk Factors and Clinical Implications-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Sleep Res. 2026;35(4):e70333. PMID 41905893. doi:10.1111/jsr.70333.
rows.implementationProposition: In adults with established bronchiectasis, polysomnography-confirmed obstructive sleep apnea is substantially more prevalent than in the general population; this supports screening and a population-level association only.
rows.finalProposition: In adults with established bronchiectasis, polysomnography-confirmed obstructive sleep apnea is substantially more prevalent than in the general population; this supports screening and a population-level association only.
rows.implementationPhenotypeRestriction: established bronchiectasis with separately diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea
rows.finalPhenotypeRestriction: established bronchiectasis with separately diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea
rows.implementationGuard: Do not infer obstructive sleep apnea from bronchiectasis alone. Require a separate obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis. Preserve obesity, craniofacial or anatomic upper-airway factors, age, sex, medication exposure, other sleep-disordered-breathing causes, and conventional obstructive sleep apnea risk factors. Association evidence must not be presented as individual causation.
rows.finalGuard: Do not infer obstructive sleep apnea from bronchiectasis alone. Require a separate obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis. Preserve obesity, craniofacial or anatomic upper-airway factors, age, sex, medication exposure, other sleep-disordered-breathing causes, and conventional obstructive sleep apnea risk factors. Association evidence must not be presented as individual causation.
rows.independentReviewFinding: Supports a population-level bronchiectasis/OSA association and screening relevance; does not establish individual causation.
rows.independentGuardCheck: Implemented separate-OSA-diagnosis requirement and conventional OSA confounder protections remain necessary and sufficient.

rows.sourceTitle: Effects of Treatment with L-Thyroxine on Chronic Urticaria in Subjects with Autoimmune Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.implementationCitation: Bordoni M, Ciarloni A, Aboud N, Sidori E, Silvetti F, Taccaliti A, Vassallo A, Romeo M, Salvio G, Balercia G. Effects of Treatment with L-Thyroxine on Chronic Urticaria in Subjects with Autoimmune Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Int J Mol Sci. 2026;27(14):6348. PMID 42511690. doi:10.3390/ijms27146348.
rows.finalCitation: Bordoni M, Ciarloni A, Aboud N, Sidori E, Silvetti F, Taccaliti A, Vassallo A, Romeo M, Salvio G, Balercia G. Effects of Treatment with L-Thyroxine on Chronic Urticaria in Subjects with Autoimmune Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Int J Mol Sci. 2026;27(14):6348. PMID 42511690. doi:10.3390/ijms27146348.
rows.implementationProposition: Chronic urticaria is frequently associated with autoimmune thyroiditis, while pathogenesis and the benefit of thyroid-directed treatment remain uncertain; this evidence supports association only.
rows.finalProposition: Chronic urticaria is frequently associated with autoimmune thyroiditis, while pathogenesis and the benefit of thyroid-directed treatment remain uncertain; this evidence supports association only.
rows.implementationPhenotypeRestriction: autoimmune thyroiditis only, with separately established chronic urticaria
rows.finalPhenotypeRestriction: autoimmune thyroiditis only, with separately established chronic urticaria
rows.implementationGuard: Require autoimmune thyroiditis and chronic urticaria to be independently established. Do not generalize from nonspecific thyroiditis, do not infer that autoimmune thyroiditis individually causes urticaria, and do not use levothyroxine response as proof of causation.
rows.finalGuard: Require autoimmune thyroiditis and chronic urticaria to be independently established. Do not generalize from nonspecific thyroiditis, do not infer that autoimmune thyroiditis individually causes urticaria, and do not use levothyroxine response as proof of causation.
rows.independentReviewFinding: Supports the implemented association between autoimmune thyroiditis and chronic urticaria while explicitly leaving pathogenesis and treatment benefit uncertain.
rows.independentGuardCheck: Implemented autoimmune-thyroiditis plus chronic-urticaria phenotype restriction and association-only language remain necessary and sufficient.

rows.sourceTitle: Pharmacological treatment for Charcot neuroarthropathy: a systematic review
rows.implementationCitation: Liu L, Lu J, Wang J, Wang Q, Zhao H, Zhang Y. Pharmacological treatment for Charcot neuroarthropathy: a systematic review. BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2026;27(1):592. PMID 42141385. doi:10.1186/s12891-026-09965-w.
rows.finalCitation: Liu L, Lu J, Wang J, Wang Q, Zhao H, Zhang Y. Pharmacological treatment for Charcot neuroarthropathy: a systematic review. BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2026;27(1):592. PMID 42141385. doi:10.1186/s12891-026-09965-w.
rows.implementationProposition: Charcot neuroarthropathy can progress to foot deformity and ulceration, creating a clinically recognized pathway to deep infection and osteomyelitis; use of this relationship requires documented wound or infection chronology.
rows.finalProposition: Charcot neuroarthropathy can progress to foot deformity and ulceration, creating a clinically recognized pathway to deep infection and osteomyelitis; use of this relationship requires documented wound or infection chronology.
rows.implementationPhenotypeRestriction: Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot, especially neuropathic or diabetic Charcot foot, with a separately established osteomyelitis diagnosis
rows.finalPhenotypeRestriction: Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot, especially neuropathic or diabetic Charcot foot, with a separately established osteomyelitis diagnosis
rows.implementationGuard: Require established Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot plus documented deformity with ulceration, soft-tissue breakdown, wound infection, or compatible deep-infection chronology before using the osteomyelitis pathway. Osteomyelitis must be separately diagnosed. Preserve diabetes, neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, trauma or surgery, wound-care history, and other infection risk factors.
rows.finalGuard: Require established Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot plus documented deformity with ulceration, soft-tissue breakdown, wound infection, or compatible deep-infection chronology before using the osteomyelitis pathway. Osteomyelitis must be separately diagnosed. Preserve diabetes, neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, trauma or surgery, wound-care history, and other infection risk factors.
rows.independentReviewFinding: The abstract expressly describes Charcot neuroarthropathy progressing to foot deformity, ulceration and osteomyelitis; the implemented wound/deep-infection-mediated pathway is conservative.
rows.independentGuardCheck: Implemented requirement for Charcot foot plus ulceration/soft-tissue breakdown/wound infection or compatible deep-infection chronology, with separate osteomyelitis diagnosis, remains necessary and sufficient.

rows.sourceTitle: Ocular findings in patients with lyme disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis

rows.finalCitation: Barbosa LIT, Lima RV, Moreira JLML, Hira S, Arruda MP, Zinher MT, Thomaz S, Del Valle GS. Ocular findings in patients with lyme disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Graefes Arch Clin Exp Ophthalmol. 2026;264(4):1101-1110. PMID 41546697. doi:10.1007/s00417-025-07110-2.
rows.implementationProposition: Uveitis, including anterior, intermediate and posterior forms, is among documented ocular manifestations reported in patients with Lyme disease.
rows.finalProposition: Uveitis, including anterior, intermediate and posterior forms, is among documented ocular manifestations reported in patients with Lyme disease.
rows.implementationPhenotypeRestriction: established Lyme disease or Lyme borreliosis context with separately diagnosed uveitis
rows.finalPhenotypeRestriction: established Lyme disease or Lyme borreliosis context with separately diagnosed uveitis
rows.implementationGuard: Require Lyme disease or Lyme borreliosis and uveitis to be independently established. Preserve other infectious, autoimmune, medication-related, traumatic, and ophthalmic etiologies. Population-level manifestation evidence does not by itself establish an individual nexus.
rows.finalGuard: Require Lyme disease or Lyme borreliosis and uveitis to be independently established. Preserve other infectious, autoimmune, medication-related, traumatic, and ophthalmic etiologies. Population-level manifestation evidence does not by itself establish an individual nexus.
rows.independentReviewFinding: The 21-study review/meta-analysis identifies anterior, intermediate and posterior uveitis among ocular manifestations of Lyme disease.
rows.independentGuardCheck: Implemented requirement for established Lyme disease and a separately diagnosed uveitis phenotype, with alternative ophthalmic etiologies preserved, remains appropriate.

rows.sourceTitle: Narcolepsy and metabolic disease: A meta-analytic synthesis
rows.implementationCitation: Zhang X, Yin W, Ren J, Zhou X, Zha M, Zong Q, Shen Y, Spruyt K, Zhou J. Narcolepsy and metabolic disease: A meta-analytic synthesis. Sleep Med Rev. 2026;87:102264. PMID 41747645. doi:10.1016/j.smrv.2026.102264.
rows.finalCitation: Zhang X, Yin W, Ren J, Zhou X, Zha M, Zong Q, Shen Y, Spruyt K, Zhou J. Narcolepsy and metabolic disease: A meta-analytic synthesis. Sleep Med Rev. 2026;87:102264. PMID 41747645. doi:10.1016/j.smrv.2026.102264.
rows.implementationProposition: Hypertension is among the cardiometabolic comorbidities reported in narcolepsy, with greater cardiometabolic burden particularly in narcolepsy type 1; this supports association and screening relevance only.
rows.finalProposition: Hypertension is among the cardiometabolic comorbidities reported in narcolepsy, with greater cardiometabolic burden particularly in narcolepsy type 1; this supports association and screening relevance only.
rows.implementationPhenotypeRestriction: established narcolepsy with separately diagnosed hypertension; association appears strongest in narcolepsy type 1
rows.finalPhenotypeRestriction: established narcolepsy with separately diagnosed hypertension; association appears strongest in narcolepsy type 1
rows.implementationGuard: Require separately diagnosed hypertension. Preserve obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, metabolic syndrome, stimulant or other medication exposure, age, sex, renal or endocrine causes, and other conventional hypertension risk factors. Do not state or imply individual causation from the meta-analysis alone.
rows.finalGuard: Require separately diagnosed hypertension. Preserve obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, metabolic syndrome, stimulant or other medication exposure, age, sex, renal or endocrine causes, and other conventional hypertension risk factors. Do not state or imply individual causation from the meta-analysis alone.
rows.independentReviewFinding: The 54-study meta-analysis reports hypertension among cardiometabolic comorbidities of narcolepsy, with greater burden particularly in narcolepsy type 1; this is association/screening evidence only.
rows.independentGuardCheck: Implemented separate-hypertension requirement and protection for obesity, OSA, metabolic syndrome, medications and other conventional hypertension causes remains necessary and sufficient.
